description:
Hello, world.

When we send spacecraft across the solar system, they never come home. Relics is an interactive web app built for NASA’s "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge to share their stories.

It brings 13 Moon, Mars, and Deep Space missions to life through storytelling, an interactive landing-site map, and a trivia quiz hosted by Moonling, Marsling, and Deepling.

Millions of miles away, none of them are forgotten.
summary:
Out there on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space, dozens of NASA machines went quiet years ago. Their stories are buried under coordinates and technical jargon, so most students and everyday people never connect with them. Relics makes learning about them fun and personal.
It tells the stories of 13 real missions, from Surveyor 3 on the Moon to InSight on Mars and Kepler in deep space, using NASA’s own photos and facts checked against NASA sources. A live clock counts how long each silent machine has been quiet. An interactive map shows where each one rests, and a quiz with mascots that cheer you on turns what you’ve read into a game. As you scroll, the page changes colour from Moon to Mars to deep space, so you feel the journey.
Relics turns forgotten hardware into characters people care about. These machines are silent, but they are not forgotten.
details:
To this day, dozens of brave rovers, landers, and probes rest silently across the Moon, Mars, and deep space—silent monuments to human curiosity. Yet because their journeys are often buried under dense coordinates and technical jargon, it is hard for young audiences and everyday people to truly connect with the amazing stories we left behind. I built RELICS because space history shouldn't feel like a textbook.

What It Does & How It Works
RELICS transforms raw NASA data into living, bite-sized stories that kids, students, and curious minds can actually feel. When you visit the site, you explore space across four simple features:

  • Color-Coded Stories: As you scroll from the Moon to Mars to deep space, the page changes color with each new world. You can tap any of 13 historic machines to read its story, see its real NASA photo, and find its actual last signal.
  • Live Silence Clocks: You can stand beside each silent machine and watch a live clock count how long it has been quiet, from years all the way down to seconds.
  • Interactive Maps: You can pick your world—the Moon or Mars—and tap a glowing pin to see exactly where a machine landed and what became of it.
  • Playful Quiz: Three friendly creature guides test what you’ve discovered. They cheer when you’re right and encourage you when you’re wrong, and every single answer comes with a real NASA fact.

Benefits & Intended Impact
By pairing simple Moon and Mars maps with bite-sized mission stories and clean visual storytelling, RELICS turns intimidating space archives into an exciting adventure for kids, students, and families. My goal is to spark curiosity and remind explorers that the rovers and probes across the Moon, Mars, and deep space are living monuments to human discovery.

How It Was Built & Tools Used

  • Data & Media: RELICS was built using verified mission records, landing coordinates, and official spacecraft photography from NASA Space Apps Challenge resources—including NASA NSSDCA, NASA mission pages, NASA / JPL-Caltech, and the NASA History Office (Beyond Earth by Asif Siddiqi).
  • Coding & AI Disclosure: The website was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (hosted on Netlify with source code on GitHub). In full transparency, Claude AI assisted with NASA dataset analysis, drafting and fact-checking the story text, and coding the website, maps, and quiz under my direction, while Gemini assisted with organizing the presentation structure. All project vision, the choice of the 13 machines, the NASA sources, and the final assembly are my own work.

What’s Next
Looking ahead, I plan to expand RELICS by adding more historic spacecraft, real NASA rover audio clips, and extra quiz levels—so the next generation keeps listening to the machines we left behind.
